title: Gift Wrap Roll

adjustment.analysis: No events, promotions, or price changes in the target week. The baseline median (2.7) is already adjusted for recent trends and seasonality. The past Mother's Day week (2026-05-04) sold 2 units, matching the baseline, and Easter (2026-03-30) had a spike but was driven by the holiday. No evidence of a lasting post-promotion dip or uplift beyond noise. The classical uplift model's 1.00 suggests no systematic driver. Noise-adjusted promotion effects are neutral. The product shows high ordinary-week volatility (97%), so no adjustment is justified.

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-97% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
